appScreening.rule: Screening classifier, not the papers' regime definition. Inputs: normalised enthalpy dH/h_s = eta*P / (rho*cp_s*max(50, T_liq-T0)*sqrt(pi*alpha_s*v*r^3)) (same form as lpbf_thermal_solver.py, flat-plate absorptivity_IR of the material authority, solid k/cp, r = d/2) and the dataset's own balling flag. balling == 1 -> 'balling-flagged' (Hofmann only); otherwise dH/h_s < 15 -> 'conduction', 15 <= dH/h_s < 30 -> 'transition', >= 30 -> 'keyhole'. Measured D/W is recorded next to the label but not used for it.

caveats: Depth is the VAPOR-DEPRESSION (keyhole) depth from operando x-ray radiographs, mean of > 30 frames, error bar = SD (Fig. 3 caption, p. 2). It is not the post-mortem melt-pool depth.

Values digitized from the embedded 300 ppi raster of Fig. 3: axes calibrated on the tick marks; value = marker centre; SD = half the error-bar span only where the bar extends beyond the marker (else blank). Read uncertainty 4 um, 6 um in crowded clusters; power read uncertainty 3 W. Powers fall on a ~13/26 W setpoint grid (cf. the Fig. 2A/B legends) but the read value is recorded, not snapped.

Regime labels for the 95 um spot come from the Fig. 3A dashed lines (blue: vapor-depression transition, red: melt-pool transition; text p. 2: below blue = conduction domain, above red = keyhole domain). The lines were measured in the stationary-beam experiment and placed in P-V space by the authors; Fig. 3A applies to the 95 um spot only, so 140 um rows carry no regime label.
Some 400-900 mm/s high-power points have a 'J'-shaped depression (text p. 2); the plotted depth is used as is.

relations.text: Ke = eta*P / ((Tl - T0) * pi * rho * Cp * sqrt(alpha * Vs * r0^3)); r0 = laser spot radius; eta = keyhole absorptivity (Eq. 6)
conduction Ke < 1.4; transition 1.4 <= Ke <= 6.0; keyhole Ke > 6.0
Ke < 16: small fluctuation, almost no porosity; Ke > 30: chaotic, unstable keyhole
eta = 0.7 * (1 - exp(-0.6 * Ke_m * Ld*)); Ke_m*Ld* = eta_m*P / ((Tl - T0) * pi * rho * Cp * Vs * r0^2); eta_m = flat-surface (minimum) absorptivity from Ye et al. 2019

relations.locator: Methods Eqs. (1)-(2), pp. 8-9; hm values p. 4
relations.text: dH/hm = beta*P / (hm*sqrt(pi*alpha_l*v*r^3)); Lth* = sqrt(alpha_l*r/v)/r; hm = rho_l*c_l*T_l; product = beta*P/(sqrt(pi)*hm*v*r^2) (alpha cancels)
relations.uncertainty: beta and liquid properties: Supplementary Table 3 (not read)

relations.text: Ti-6Al-4V stable -> unstable keyhole at dH/hm*Lth* ~ 8 +/- 3 (~60 deg front wall angle), from Cunningham 2019 and Zhao 2020 data

relations.locator: p. 3 last paragraph; p. 5 (keyhole width fluctuation paragraph)
relations.text: Al7A77 stable -> unstable at dH/hm*Lth* ~ 20 +/- 3 (~80 deg); fluctuation regimes I < 10, II 10-20, III > 20
secondary citation: King et al. found the conduction -> keyhole transition at dH/hm ~ 30 +/- 4 for 316L
dH_max/hs = eta*P / (rho*hs*sqrt(pi*alpha*sigma^3*U)) (Eq. 4 with S'=0, Fo << 1); sigma = half-width of the Gaussian beam at the surface (Table 1)
delta* = 0 (dH <= hs); sqrt(dH/hs - 1) (hs <= dH <= Hv); sqrt(dH/hs - 10) (dH > Hv) AS PRINTED; delta* = depth/sigma
relations.uncertainty: error < +/-10% claimed; the printed form does not reproduce the paper's own Table 3/4 pairs (see report)

relations.text: keyhole transition at dH/hs = Hv/hs (Richard's and Trouton's rules); Hv/hs = 10 (generic), 10.62 (304 SS), 10.22 (V), 12.34 (Ti-6Al-4V)
stationary-beam drill rate grows ~linearly with power density above ~0.4 MW/cm2; rho = 2P/(pi*D^2)
relations.uncertainty: stationary beam, not a moving-beam regime boundary

relations.text: melt-pool transition when the melt-pool depth-to-width aspect ratio reaches ~0.5 (varies with power)
low-PV keyhole-pore energy-density threshold Ec ~ 3.7 MJ/m2; high-PV d_c ~ E with slope 50 cm3/MJ (bare and powder), intercepts ~100 um apart; d_c ~ V^6 and d_c ~ P
relations.uncertainty: definition of E is in the Supplementary Materials (not read)
